glosses: An electrical device for toasting food, typically sliced bread.
A toasting fork.
A fish ready for toasting.

examples.text: [T]he tumult of the thousand different cries of the eager dealers, all shouting at the top of their voices, at one and the same time, is almost bewildering. […] "Come and look at 'em! here's toasters!" bellows one with a Yarmouth bloater stuck on a toasting-fork.

glosses: One who toasts (cooks lightly by browning).
One who toasts (engages in salute while drinking alcohol).
A firearm, especially a pistol.

examples.text: The renegade, you been afraid I penetrate pop culture / Bring 'em a lot closer to the block where they pop toasters

glosses: A rapier or similar weapon.

examples.text: This attitude, and the sight of the blade which glistened by moonlight in his face, checked in some sort, the ardour of his assailant, who desired he would lay aside his toaster, and take a bout with him at equal arms.

glosses: Any of several small, box-like automobiles exemplified by the Scion xB and Honda Element.
An electronic organ, especially a crude one that uses analog technology.
A low-end or outdated personal computer.

examples.text: For most older computers (pre-486 and even some 486s), it's simply easier to throw them away and start over (and cheaper, too). I know; this probably goes against the grain; after all, you hung onto that old toaster for three years, and now it makes a darn good doorstop.
On the technical side, we had only the old “toaster” Macintosh computers as our environment (only black and white and 512 by 480 screen resolution) and a variety of IBM PCs or equivalents.

glosses: A protogen.
A self-contained software package distributable over the Internet or by burning onto CDs.

examples.text: The Freedom Toaster was developed with backing from Mark Shuttleworth as a vending-machine-style dispenser of free digital products, including Ubuntu Linux.

glosses: A disc jockey who accompanies reggae music with improvised rhythmic speech.
Diesel locomotives built by GE Transportation known for a propensity to catch fire, especially those showing previous fire damage.

examples.text: No. 4020 shows off the aftereffects of the GE “toaster” phenomenon as it runs on the Joint Line north of the Air Force Academy (7/02/2023).
Railfans often call GE Dash-9s as "toasters" which certainly applies to this locomotive.

glosses: An EMD AEM-7 electric locomotive

examples.text: The origin of the design led railroaders to dub the units “meatballs,” and its boxy appearance inspired railfans to call them “toasters.”

Sometimes affectionately referred to as “toasters” and “Swedish meatballs” due to their compact, boxy design and Swedish origins, the AEM-7s first entered service in May 1980 and since then have traveled more than 220 million miles.

Par son itinéraire, et celui de quelques autres, le roman met en scène l’« approximation existentielle » d’hommes et de femmes désemparées dans une société en perte d’humanité, qui se débarrasse des éclopés comme « des cafetières déglinguées, des grille-pain en panne ». Mais les grille-pain, eux, n’ont pas besoin de se sentir vivants.
